rationale: class_prevalence gives positive/negative counts, prevalence and imbalance ratio with the required fraud_prevalence.png. feature_comparison drops the catalogue default fraud_pattern_type: the manifest shows it null in 12198 of 12845 rows, i.e. populated only for the ~647 flagged claims, so it encodes the label. All member_* joined features are excluded: member_sex, member_race_ethnicity and member_age_band are protected attributes named by the task, and member_payer_type is a close proxy for age and income; this keeps the comparison to claim-level fields and avoids the member join entirely. Selected features are legitimately available claim attributes not derived from the label: five categorical fields (claim_type, cpt_category, place_of_service, provider_specialty, network_status) plus three binary flags (er_flag, auth_required_flag, high_cost_flag) reported as shares, and five numeric fields (billed/allowed/paid amounts, service_units, length_of_stay) reported as mean and median since amounts are skewed. leakage_assessment is switched on (default off) because the task requires an explicit list of label-derived, identifier and protected fields and whether any appear in the plan; with the feature set above flagged_in_plan should be empty. write_report prints every rate as numerator/denominator, cites an artifact or metrics key per result bullet, and includes the caveats the task mandates: synthetic label, class imbalance, association not causation, descriptive only, small groups (flagged class is ~5% so per-value cells in high-cardinality features are small), and no operational use. sample_preview and model_limitations are omitted because no sampling or model is involved.
